# GEO report: trailhead **New to GEO?** GEO (generative engine optimization) means making your site easy for search engines and AI tools to find, read and quote. This report checks the technical basics. ## Code score: 46–54/100, At risk Confidence: High (checked 21 of 23 points). How it's calculated: low = 10.5 ÷ 23 × 100 = 46. High = (10.5 + 2) ÷ 23 × 100 = 54. Most of the score is lost to four site-wide problems. The pages are built in the browser, so crawlers get empty HTML. One page is hidden from search by a header. The sitemap line is not an absolute URL. Every page shares one title and description. The only unknown is the canonical address (GEO-015), because no domain is declared in a config. I assumed you want search and AI tools to find this site. All results are read from code. ## Live check - **Not run.** To add it, give me your site's URL. ## Do these first ### 1. Turn on server rendering so pages arrive as real HTML - **Why it matters:** with `ssr: false`, crawlers get an empty shell and have to run JavaScript to see any text, which many don't do. - **Where:** `nuxt.config.ts:2` - **What the code says:** `ssr: false,` - **Size:** Small - **Score after this:** 59–67 ### 2. Make the sitemap line in robots.txt an absolute URL - **Why it matters:** the sitemap standard asks for a full address, and crawlers may ignore a relative one. - **Where:** `public/robots.txt:4` - **What the code says:** `Sitemap: /sitemap.xml` - **Size:** Small - **Score after this:** 54–63 ### 3. Link to the guides page with a real link - **Why it matters:** `/guides` is reached only by a button that navigates with JavaScript. Crawlers follow `` links and won't find this page that way. - **Where:** `pages/index.vue:8` - **What the code says:** `` - **Size:** Small - **Score after this:** 54–63 ## All results | Rule | What it checks | Code | Where | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | GEO-013 | robots.txt valid and reachable | Clear | `public/robots.txt`, valid lines, tiny file | | GEO-009 | Search crawlers allowed | Clear | `public/robots.txt:1-2`, only `/admin` blocked | | GEO-014 | Routes are indexable | Problem | `server/middleware/headers.ts:3`, `/guides` is noindex (1 of 2 routes clear) | | GEO-015 | Absolute canonical on own domain | Can't tell | No canonical set; no declared site origin | | GEO-003 | Content in server HTML | Problem | `nuxt.config.ts:2`, site-wide | | GEO-004 | JSON-LD valid | Not applicable | No JSON-LD found | | GEO-011 | Valid, discoverable sitemap | Problem | `public/robots.txt:4`, relative Sitemap line | | GEO-012 | Title, description, lang | Problem | `app.vue:2`, one shared title and description on both routes; `lang` is set | | GEO-016 | Server-rendered links | Problem | `pages/index.vue:8`, `/guides` only via `router.push` | | GEO-017 | No snippet blocking | Clear | No `nosnippet` or `max-snippet:0` in head or `headers.ts` | | GEO-002 | Accessibility basics | Clear | Read all three pages and `app.vue`; no images, button has text | | GEO-101 | App association files | Not applicable | No mobile app declared | | GEO-010 | llms.txt (info only) | Not applicable | Not present; not scored | | GEO-102 | App structured data (info only) | Not applicable | Not scored | ## Other problems found - **The sitemap lists a page the server marks noindex.** `public/sitemap.xml:4` has `https://trailhead.example/guides`, and `server/middleware/headers.ts:3` has `setResponseHeader(event, 'X-Robots-Tag', 'noindex');` for `/guides`. Remove the header rule if you want the guides indexed. That looks like the intent, since the page is in the sitemap and in the navigation. - **The sitemap host looks like a placeholder.** `public/sitemap.xml:3` uses `https://trailhead.example/`. Replace it with your real domain. ## Worth considering - **The guides page promises routes but lists none:** `pages/guides.vue:4`: `

Routes graded from easy to strenuous.

`. Add the actual routes with their grades as text. Giving each route its own page and address would let it be found and linked individually. - **The home page has almost no text:** `pages/index.vue:7`: `

Walks across the Peak District

`. Add a sentence or two on what walks you cover, and link to a few of them. - **Every page shares one title and description:** `app.vue:2`: `useHead({ title: 'Trailhead' })`. Give each page its own, for example "Trail guides – Peak District walks | Trailhead". - **No canonical address and no site URL in the config:** `nuxt.config.ts:3-8`: only `htmlAttrs` and `meta` are set. Declare your domain and add a canonical link on each page. - **Nothing states who the site is in a machine-readable way:** no JSON-LD in any file I read. Add `WebSite` or `Organization` markup with the site name and URL. - **Sitemap has no ``:** `public/sitemap.xml:3-4`. Add dates once you have real update dates. A generator such as `@nuxtjs/sitemap` could keep the file in sync. ## Can't tell from code - **GEO-015 (canonical):** I need your real domain. Once I have it, I can check whether the canonical points at it. - **Bot protection:** code can't show whether a CDN or firewall lets real crawlers through. Run `geopilot logs `, which checks real crawlers against their published addresses. - **Hosting headers:** any extra `X-Robots-Tag` headers set outside this repository are not visible here. ## Assumptions - You want search engines and AI search tools to find this site, because there is no `geo.config.json`. - `/admin` is deliberately private. It has noindex and a robots Disallow, and I left both alone. - `trailhead.example` is a placeholder domain. ## What to do next 1. Run the geopilot `fix` command to apply item 1. You'll see every change before anything is written. 2. Run the geopilot `explain` command with any rule id, such as `GEO-014`, to learn more. 3. For proof from a running site, ask for a live scan with its URL. Technical readiness only. GEO does not measure or predict citations, rankings, traffic or inclusion in any AI or search product.
